quote: SOCS3 small interfering RNA knockdown and SOCS3 deletion in astrocytes augmented the synergistic effect of IL-6 and IL-17 due to an enhancement of activation of the NF-kappaB and MAPK pathways.
summary: In astrocytes (CNS, not gut), SOCS3 knockdown or deletion enhanced IL-17/IL-6 inflammatory signalling, so SOCS3 acts as a negative feedback regulator.

quote: EE was operationally defied as enteric inflammation measured by any one of the fecal biomarkers reg1B, alpha-1-antitrypsin, MPO, calprotectin, or neopterin.
summary: Fecal reg1B was one of several markers used to define environmental enteropathy in Bangladeshi infants; no UC data.

quote: Moreover, IL-22 induced expression of host defense genes (such as REG1A, REG1B, and DMBT1) in enterocytes, goblet cells, Paneth cells, Tuft cells, and even stem cells.
summary: In human small intestinal organoids, IL-22 induced REG1B expression across epithelial cell types.

quote: Immunohistochemistry against known cell-type markers on serial sections has localised the expression of REGs to metaplastic Paneth cells (REG1A, REG1B and REG3A) and enteroendocrine cells (REG4), with a marked expansion of expression during inflammation.
summary: REG1B expression localises to metaplastic Paneth cells in colonic mucosa and expands during inflammation in IBD.

quote: Upregulated genes in CD included SAA1 (fold change [FC] +7.5, P = 1.47 × 10(-41)) and REGL (FC +7.3, P = 2.3 × 10(-16)), whereas cellular detoxification genes including-SLC14A2 (FC-2.49, P = 0.00002) were downregulated.
summary: REGL (REG1B) was strongly upregulated (about 7-fold) in intestinal biopsies from Crohn's disease patients versus controls.

quote: The stool regenerating gene 1β (REG1B) protein, which is a putative measure of intestinal injury and repair, was tested as a noninvasive biomarker of future childhood stunting.
summary: Stool REG1B at 3 months predicted later growth shortfall in children from Bangladesh and Peru; not a UC study.

quote: SYCN, REG1B and AGR2 were also significantly elevated in PDAC compared to benign controls (p ≤ 0.01), and AGR2 was significantly elevated in PDAC compared to other cancers (p ConclusionsAdditional serum biomarkers, particularly SYCN and REG1B, when combined with CA19.9, show promise as improved diagnostic indicators of pancreatic cancer, which therefore warrants further validation.
summary: Serum REG1B was elevated in pancreatic cancer and improved diagnosis when combined with CA19.9; no UC data.

quote: The top upregulated genes in IBD are associated with diabetogenesis (REG1A, REG1B), bacterial signals (TLRs, NLRs), innate immunity (DEFA6, IDO1, EXOSC1), inflammation (CXCLs), and matrix degradation (MMPs).
summary: REG1B appears among the top upregulated genes in an IBD transcriptome signature, without a specific result.

quote: Four genes [DEFFA6, REG1B, BTNL3, OLFM4] showed DNA methylation in the absence of known CpG islands.
summary: REG1B was one of four differentially methylated genes in treatment-naive UC biopsies lacking known CpG islands.

quote: Giardia was associated with increase in Reg1b [β (SE) 72.189 (26.394), p = 0.006] and anti-flic IgA[β (SE) 0.054 (0.021), p = 0.0091].
summary: Fecal and serum Reg1b rose with enteropathogen infection in Pakistani children with environmental enteric dysfunction; no UC data.

quote: In conclusion, we identified potential hub genes, including REG3A, REG1A, DEFA6, REG1B, and DEFA5, which might be significantly associated with UC progression.
summary: REG1B is one of five genes in a logistic regression diagnostic model for UC built from biopsy transcriptomes.

quote: Reg1B was significantly higher in participants with EAEC (P=0.004) while, neopterin levels were significantly lower in ETEC (P=0.003) and Shigella/EIEC (P=0.003) positive cases.
summary: Fecal Reg1B, an enteropathy marker, was higher in children infected with EAEC in Bangladesh; not UC.

quote: The study results also corroborate that infection with Blastocystis had significant negative association with alpha-1 antitrypsin and Reg1B concentrations measured in the stool samples of the study participants.
summary: Fecal Reg1B, an enteric dysfunction marker, was inversely associated with Blastocystis infection in malnourished Bangladeshi adults; not UC.

quote: There was an overlap of 5 genes: REG1B, REG1A, MUC4, GRAMD2, and CASP10.
summary: REG1B was dysregulated in the non-inflamed terminal ileum of UC patients with both active and inactive extensive colitis versus controls.

quote: Infection with H. pylori had significant positive association with fecal AAT concentrations (Coefficient = 0.26; 95% CI = 0.02, 0.49; p-value = 0.03) and inverse relationship with Reg1B concentrations measured in the stool samples (Coefficient = -0.32; 95% CI = -0.59, -0.05; p-value = 0.02).
summary: Fecal Reg1B was inversely associated with H. pylori infection in Bangladeshi children; not a UC study.

quote: EED biomarkers included calprotectin (marker of inflammation), alpha-1 antitrypsin (intestinal permeability) and REG1B (intestinal damage).
summary: Fecal REG1B, a marker of intestinal damage, was inversely associated with gut microbiota maturity in Malawian children; not UC.

quote: Commercial ELISA kits were used to measure gut inflammatory markers Calprotectin and REG1B.
summary: Fecal REG1B was measured as a gut inflammation marker alongside miRNA levels in Bangladeshi children; no specific UC result.

quote: LCN2 correlates positively with myeloperoxidase (r=0.19, p=0.005), neopterin (r=0.20, p=0.004), calprotectin (r=0.3, p=0.0001), Reg1B (r=0.20, p=0.003) and EED score (r=0.20, p=0.003).
summary: Fecal Reg1B correlated with lipocalin-2 and inversely with LRP1 in children with environmental enteric dysfunction; not UC.

quote: CD274, CHI3L1, REG1B, ITGAV, PRSS8, ITGA11, GDF15, DEFA1_DEFA1B, and IL6 ranked highest in protein importance ordering.
summary: Plasma REG1B was one of nine proteins in a model predicting incident Crohn's disease years before diagnosis.

quote: Several of the genes, including DEFA6, PAP, REG1A, REG1B, and phospholipase A2 had been implicated in previous studies, supporting their key role in CD.
summary: REG1B is among nine genes upregulated in all four colonic Crohn's disease patients' involved tissue, mentioned in a gene list.

quote: As intestinal health markers we measured fecal calprotectin, regenerating 1B protein (REG1B) and alpha-1-antitrypsin concentrations at 18 months of age (after 12 months of supplementation) and 1 year later (12 months after cessation of supplementation).
summary: Fecal REG1B was used as an intestinal repair marker and did not differ with nutrient supplementation in Malawian children; not UC.

quote: PYY, FOXA2, REG3A, REG1A, REG1B were identified as HGs utilizing the machine learning algorithm.
summary: REG1B was one of five machine-learning-derived diagnostic hub genes for Crohn's disease with kidney stone disease, with high expression in goblet cells.

quote: Machine learning predicts relapse after anti-TNF withdrawal in ulcerative colitis using rectal biopsy transcriptomics
summary: REG1B was among the genes with highest predictive importance for relapse after anti-TNF withdrawal in a UC biopsy machine learning model.

quote: Here we identified 15 genes required for cell growth or proliferation in CD44+CD24- human breast cancer cells in a large-scale loss-of-function screen and found that inhibition of several of these (IL6, PTGIS, HAS1, CXCL3, and PFKFB3) reduced Stat3 activation.
summary: CXCL3 is one of several genes whose inhibition reduced Stat3 activation in breast cancer stem-like cells; no UC or colitis data.

quote: This paper reviews all available information on hypoxia-induced changes in the expression of all CXC chemokines (CXCL1, CXCL2, CXCL3, CXCL4, CXCL5, CXCL6, CXCL7, CXCL8 (IL-8), CXCL9, CXCL10, CXCL11, CXCL12 (SDF-1), CXCL13, CXCL14, CXCL15, CXCL16, CXCL17) as well as CXC chemokine receptors-CXCR1, CXCR2, CXCR3, CXCR4, CXCR5, CXCR6, CXCR7 and CXCR8.
summary: Review of hypoxia effects on CXC chemokines including CXCL3 in cancer; no UC content.
